instruction: My EMR cluster {{troubleshooting-multiservice-emr-0hr2dw3rz-eu-west-1-EmrClusterId}} in eu-west-1 is configured with Spark but no steps have been submitted yet. Review the Spark configuration and cluster sizing — what problems would occur when a Spark job is submitted?
expected_answer:
No Spark steps have been submitted to the cluster, so no job is currently running. However, the spark-defaults configuration has several critical problems that would prevent or severely degrade any submitted job:

1. Oversized driver memory: spark.driver.memory is set to 60G, which exceeds the total memory of an m5.2xlarge instance (32 GB). This would prevent the driver from launching at all.

2. Severe executor overallocation: spark.executor.instances is set to 425, with spark.executor.memory of 20G and spark.yarn.executor.memoryOverhead of 3G (23 GB per executor). The core instance fleet targets only 1 m5.2xlarge instance (32 GB), so YARN could provision at most 1 executor. The remaining 424 requested executors would never be allocated, leaving the vast majority of Spark tasks waiting indefinitely.

3. Dynamic allocation disabled: spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled is false, so Spark cannot scale the executor count down to match actual cluster capacity.

4. Excessive shuffle partitions: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is set to 3000, which adds unnecessary scheduling overhead relative to the 1 available executor.

To fix: reduce spark.driver.memory below 32G, set spark.executor.instances to match the core fleet capacity (or enable dynamic allocation), and reduce spark.sql.shuffle.partitions — or scale the core instance fleet up to provide the requested executor capacity.
